description: TACT organizes ESL tutoring as a pedagogical decision space connecting learner-state annotation, tutor-strategy selection, and next-turn response generation.
title: TACT dual-taxonomy framework for annotating tutoring moves and conditional feedback strategies

description: TAME is a statistical method for detecting treatment effects in randomized controlled experiments run inside online tutoring systems.
title: TAME (detecting treatment effects by training a model across multiple experiments and testing residuals)

description: The target trial framework requires researchers \"to explicitly state the hypothetical trial they want to emulate with an observational study, specifying eligibility criteria, treatment strategies, follow-up period, and a time-zero\".
title: Target trial emulation framework for causal analysis of observational learning data

description: TDS is a scoring-assignment methodology in which a first rater scores every performance, and only examinees whose Rater 1 score falls within a Critical Score Range (CSR) near the pass/fail cutoff receive a second rating.
title: Targeted Double Scoring (TDS)

description: The article develops a coding framework rating each intervention 0–2 on task characteristics (varied vs repetitive, group/team/opponent vs individual, divergent vs convergent, open-ended vs technical instruction) and environment characteristics (open vs fixed space, props vs no props), averaged into
title: Task and environment creativity classification framework

description: The article organizes its findings by grouping DIGHIM assessments into broader task categories to locate where generative AI shows relative strengths versus persistent limitations.
title: Task-category taxonomy of assessment susceptibility to AI-generated content

description: The framework defines strategies as \"students’ conscious and controllable sequences of actions to facilitate and enhance task performance\", making them measurable from log data.
title: Task-oriented strategy framework for open-ended learning environments

description: The review assembles a taxonomy of validity criteria considered in TEL research, including effectiveness, statistical validity, external validity, rigour, authenticity, fairness, trustworthiness, usability and usefulness, each paired with synonyms observed in the literature (e.g., generalisability f
title: Taxonomy of 27 validity criteria for technology-enhanced learning with synonyms

description: The article organizes ACLS research around dimensions drawn from prior taxonomies: \"identify dimensions such as the timing of support (whether it is provided immediately or with some delay during the collab- oration, or before or after the collaboration), the psychological realm of support (cognitiv
title: Taxonomy of ACLS support dimensions

description: The review organizes algebra outcome measures into a taxonomy distinguishing global constructs from specific facets.
title: Taxonomy of algebraic thinking operationalizations: global measures versus specific facets

description: The article organizes philosophical, theological, and scientific perspectives on causation into three families relevant to interpreting cross-lagged panel models.
title: Taxonomy of causality theories: sequential, simultaneous, and reciprocal

description: The review organises classroom-based physical activity into three forms — active breaks, curriculum-focussed active breaks, and physically active lessons — defined as \"physical activity carried out during regular class time\", distinct from recess or lunch breaks.
title: Taxonomy of classroom-based physical activity forms and academic-related outcome categories

description: The review organizes the 54 included studies' educational interventions along stated dimensions: strategies were presented \"by serial cue or whole clinical cases that presented as process-oriented or knowledge-oriented\".
title: Taxonomy of clinical reasoning educational interventions by focus and case presentation

description: The review classifies digital learning resources into defined types used to categorize interventions: e-learning, digital assessment, social component, podcasts, blended learning, virtual patient, virtual reality, augmented reality, and serious/educational games.
title: Taxonomy of digital learning resource types for prescribing education

description: The review organizes the educational AI literature by intervention type, finding that studies \"address the potential of EAI on student performance through applications (n = 8), simulations (n = 8), VR (n = 4) and AR (n = 2)\".
title: Taxonomy of EAI modalities in education

description: Table S1 organizes quantifiable text characteristics by linguistic level: sounds in words (number of phonemes, phonemic Levenshtein distance, internal phonemic predictability), word structure (decoding demand, orthographic Levenshtein distance, syllables, sight words), word meaning (age of acquisiti
title: Taxonomy of early-grades text characteristics organized by linguistic level from sounds to text density

description: The article assembles a taxonomy of FOI components drawn from Dane and Schneider (1998) and Durlak and DuPre (2008).
title: Taxonomy of eight fidelity-of-implementation components

description: The review organizes the school-based self-management literature by the specific intervention configuration employed, distinguishing approaches such as prompted self-monitoring, self-monitoring plus reinforcement based on both accuracy and performance, and prompted self-monitoring plus graphing.
title: Taxonomy of eight primary self-management intervention configurations

description: From a review of 28 manuscripts defining computational thinking, the authors identified five key CT aspects in the context of modeling: decomposing problems so they are computationally solvable, creating artifacts using algorithmic thinking, generating/organizing/interpreting data, testing and debug
title: Taxonomy of five computational thinking aspects with 13 sub-aspects

description: Using a Lakatosian framework of research programs, the article categorizes SR research into four traditions, each with a hard core of foundational assertions protected by a belt of auxiliary hypotheses and methods.
title: Taxonomy of four SR research traditions distinguished by core explanatory construct families and Lakatosian hard cores

description: The review organizes the gamified TEFL literature around a taxonomy of game elements, counting the frequency with which each appears across the 33 included studies: \"Feedback	23\", challenge, points, leaderboard, leveling, time, badge, progress bar, story/narration, digital badges, avatar/character,
title: Taxonomy of gamification elements in TEFL applications

description: The article presents a taxonomy of indicators for characterizing group and individual behaviour in CSCL, based on three perspectives: the group in relation to similar groups, an individual in relation to his/her colleagues, and the group itself.
title: Taxonomy of indicators characterizing group and individual behaviour in CSCL from three perspectives

description: The article synthesizes fragmented prior characterizations of AI code completion interactions into a unified taxonomy of behavioral metrics.
title: Taxonomy of interaction behaviors with AI code suggestions

description: The review introduces a classification (its Fig.
title: Taxonomy of item difficulty prediction approaches: expert-driven versus machine-driven

description: The article defines a knowledge component as 'an acquired unit of cognitive function or structure that can be inferred from performance on a set of related tasks' and classifies KCs along four dimensions: whether task features and response are constant or variable, whether the feature-response relat
title: Taxonomy of knowledge components classified by task features, response, relationship, and rationale

description: The review describes the family of questionnaires used to measure learning approaches: Biggs' Study Process Questionnaire (SPQ), whose strategic approach is termed the achieving approach; its revision, the R-SPQ-2F, which \"uses fewer items to narrow in on solely the deep and surface approaches\"; Ent
title: Taxonomy of learning-approaches measurement inventories (SPQ, R-SPQ-2F, ASI, ALSI, ASSIST)

description: The review organizes the heterogeneous payoff systems used in post-decision wagering into two broad classes: four-cell matrices, where a low and a high wager option combine with correct and incorrect responses to yield four possible outcomes, and free-choice designs with more than four cells.
title: Taxonomy of PDW payoff schemes: four-cell matrices versus free-choice designs

description: The paper defines pedagogical sycophancy as pressure-contingent validation of a misconception after the tutor is pushed to agree, distinguishing it from ordinary factual error.
title: Taxonomy of pedagogical sycophancy

description: The article's methodological contribution is a taxonomy of structural equation models for directional ordering, extending Muthén and Asparouhov's contemporaneous-effects models with latent measurement factors, lag2 paths, random intercepts, and covariate strategies.
title: Taxonomy of reciprocal effect panel models: CLPM, RI-CLPM, PCPM, and CCLPM with lag0, lag1, and lag2 effects

description: The review organises teachers' classroom humour into seven styles drawn from the included literature: course-related, course-unrelated, affiliative, aggressive, self-enhancing, self-defeating, and festive humour.
title: Taxonomy of seven teacher humour styles and three affiliative sub-styles

description: The survey organises the field of student free-text evaluation — the automatic evaluation of students' free-text production including short answers and essays — along two axes.
title: Taxonomy of student free-text evaluation

description: The paper organizes its analysis into distinct types of teacher intervention during rounds: ratifying pupils' work, reminding pupils of neglected task aspects, making suggestions, maintaining classroom control, and making whole-class announcements.
title: Taxonomy of teacher intervention types during “making rounds” in computer-based collaborative learning

description: The review classifies the pedagogical approaches reported in RSE studies into categories including multiple strategies, health promotion, delivery personnel, a suite of active learning pedagogies, cross-curriculum approaches, UNESCO guidance, philosophy/ethics, and sex/gender-based approaches.
title: Taxonomy of teaching approaches used to deliver school-based RSE

description: The paper organizes approaches to using student test scores for school evaluation into distinct estimator families.
title: Taxonomy of test-score-based school evaluation estimators
